Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker

Class PickerSpawnService

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker.PickerSpawnService
public final class PickerSpawnService extends Object
Authoring aid behind /sg spawnall: spawns one of every mob that could wear googly eyes — every summonable living entity, whether or not it has an eye config yet — so the picker can be used on any of them without hunting each one down in survival. The single-mob sibling /sg spawn <type> lands in spawnOne(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.world.entity.EntityType<?>). The ender dragon (ServerEyeConfigs.ENDER_DRAGON) is skipped: it's hard-excluded from eyes, and NoAi doesn't subdue it (its flight/phase logic ignores the flag), so spawning one wrecks the grid. Both verbs also skip any type an admin listed in the server config's spawnExcludedMods / spawnExcludedEntities (ServerConfig.isSpawnExcluded(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation)).

The server-owned /sg spawn and /sg spawnall commands call spawn(ServerPlayer, String) / spawnOne(ServerPlayer, EntityType) on the server thread, so the verbs work from a remote client as well as in single-player.

Layout: mobs are grouped by mod, sorted by id within each mod. Each mod gets its own row heading in the cardinal direction nearest the player's facing (mobs spaced one cell apart), and each subsequent mod's row is shifted one cell counter-clockwise. Spawned mobs have their AI disabled, sit on the ground, face the player, and water-dwellers get a small water pocket. (Whether they actually show eyes still follows the server spawn-chance config; toggle the picker on to force eyes.)

If the player is standing over air when the command runs, the per-cell terrain is ignored and the whole grid is laid on a flat sandstone floor at the player's level — a 5x5 tile under each mob, with water mobs getting a walled 3x3 basin instead. This is a throwaway-test-world convenience and freely overwrites whatever blocks it lands on.

  • Method Details

    • spawn

      public static void spawn(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, String modFilter)
      Spawn the grid around player (must run on the server thread). Reports the result.
      Parameters:
      modFilter - if non-null/blank, only spawn mobs whose namespace equals it (e.g. "minecraft" or "exoticbirds"), and additionally report each type in that namespace that was dropped and why — a debugging aid for mods whose mobs don't appear.

    • spawnOne

      public static void spawnOne(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.entity.EntityType<?> type)
      Spawn a single type at the block the player is targeting (within 20.0 blocks) — the /sg spawn <type> server-thread half. Shares spawnall's conventions (NoAi + persistent, facing the player, ender dragon excluded) but never terraforms: water mobs spawn wherever the player aims, so aim into water to keep one alive. Fails with feedback when no block is targeted or the mob's bounding box doesn't fit at the target.

    • prepareForCommandSpawn

      public static void prepareForCommandSpawn(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity entity, double x, double y, double z, float yaw)
      Put an entity at its destination and complete the normal command-spawn lifecycle before applying the picker's frozen display state. Some modded mobs leave required persistent fields unset until Mob.finalizeSpawn(net.minecraft.world.level.ServerLevelAccessor, net.minecraft.world.DifficultyInstance, net.minecraft.world.entity.EntitySpawnReason, net.minecraft.world.entity.SpawnGroupData); inserting a factory-created mob without this step can make it impossible to save. Public for the shared GameTest regression check, which lives in another module.
